newsitem.title: USA: Ranks of AMR pilots' union fractured -NYT.
newsitem.headline: Ranks of AMR pilots' union fractured -NYT.

text.p: The union for the 9,300 pilots of American Airlines is disunified and has failed to get much support from other employees at the carrier, the New York Times said Friday.
The paper quoted one American pilot as saying that he and other pilots would approve the original labour proposal if given another opportunity.
"We would pass that contract in a heartbeat if we had a second chance," pilot Walter Brown told the paper. "There is a lot of dissension within the Allied Pilots' Association (A.P.A.)."

American and the A.P.A. have failed to make any breakthroughs in their talks, which began after union members last month rejected a five percent pay rise. The latest reported offer from the airline was a six percent hike over four years.
The union has said it will come up with a new pay proposal -- probably less than the 11.5 percent over four years it had originally sought.

A strike at the nation's second-biggest carrier is scheduled to begin at midnight on Friday and would cost the U.S. economy $100 million to $200 million a day, according to one Department of Transportation estimate.
Friday's newspaper report said a two-tier wage system that gave new pilots lower pay has caused friction among pilots in the past, although union leaders are seeking to close the gap.
The report also said there was little sympathy for the pilots among other employees at American, many of whom would be laid off in the event of a strike.
It said sarcastic sheets were being circulated among some employees, including one with the acronym S.P.O.I.L.E.D. for, "Spoiled Pilots' Objective is Leaving Employees Destitute".
